# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

Every applicable rule is clear from the code. The only things the code can't show are what your server or CDN (the network in front of your site) does at runtime. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is broken. The one open question is outside the code, so it comes first.

### 1. Confirm real search crawlers get through your CDN or firewall
- **Why it matters:** The code allows crawlers, but a CDN or firewall in front of the site could still block them, and code can't show that.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` followed by `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100–100. The code score doesn't change, because that question sits outside the score. The check settles whether crawlers really arrive.
- **How:** run `geopilot logs <access log>`, or give me your URL for a live scan.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`: valid groups and a `Sitemap:` line, tiny file |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-3`: `*` is allowed except `/account`. GPTBot and ClaudeBot are blocked (lines 5-9), which matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"` in `geo.config.json`. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 sampled routes indexable. Only `app/account/page.tsx:1` has noindex, and it is deliberate and not in the sitemap or navigation. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on the declared origin | Clear | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: each is absolute and on `https://www.orchard.example` |
| GEO-003 | Primary content is in server HTML | Clear | Next.js App Router server components with no client-side fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and meets requirements | Not applicable | No `application/ld+json` or `@type` found anywhere |
| GEO-011 | Valid sitemap is discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid and listed in `public/robots.txt:11` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. The 3 indexable pages each have a title and description. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes reachable via server-rendered links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:7`: plain `<a href>` links to `/`, `/varieties` and `/visit` |
| GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions don't conflict with AI-search policy | Clear | No `nosnippet` or `max-snippet`. `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:9` is scoped to the cookie notice. |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | All 5 page files and the layout read: no images, and every link and button has text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app profile declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not scored | Not present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not scored | Not an app |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Add the address and directions to /visit:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page body only gives opening days, so the description promises directions the page doesn't deliver. Adding the address, a postcode and how to get there would match the promise.
- **Label the business with structured data:** `app/visit/page.tsx:4`: `Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October.` Once the address is on the page, LocalBusiness JSON-LD (machine-readable labels) could mark up the address and opening hours already shown. This might help machines read them.
- **Name the site in a machine-readable way:** `app/layout.tsx:1`: only `metadataBase` is set. Organization and WebSite JSON-LD with the name and URL is missing from the layout.
- **Back up "Over forty varieties":** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: `Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain.` Only two are named. A list of the varieties would support the claim.
- **Give each variety its own page:** the same line. Pages like `/varieties/ashmeads-kernel`, listed in `public/sitemap.xml`, would let people and machines land on a specific variety.
- **Add `<lastmod>` dates to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5`: the `<url>` entries have only `<loc>`. If you know when pages change, dates would help crawlers decide when to revisit.
- **Link onward from the home page:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Grown in Herefordshire since 1952.` The home page links only through the shared navigation. A sentence leading into varieties and visiting would connect the pages.
- **Add social-sharing tags:** `app/layout.tsx:1` and the page metadata set no `openGraph` values. Adding a title, description and image would improve link previews.
- **Say where the orchard is:** `app/page.tsx:1`: `title: 'Orchard: heritage apple trees'`. Adding the village or county to the title or description (the body only mentions Herefordshire) makes clear who and where it's from.
- **Build the sitemap from the framework:** `public/sitemap.xml` is hand-kept. A Next.js `app/sitemap.ts` would stay in step with new pages automatically.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live-only checks:** real status codes for `/robots.txt`, the sitemap and the pages, redirects, and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers set outside the repo. These don't change the code results. A live scan with your URL would confirm them.
- **Rule 4 (GEO-004):** not applicable because there's no JSON-LD. It will be scored once you add some.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` in `geo.config.json`.
- You want training crawlers blocked. The robots.txt groups for GPTBot and ClaudeBot match `policy.trainingCrawlers: "block"`, so they weren't counted against you.
- `/account` is deliberately private: it's disallowed in `public/robots.txt:3` and noindexed at `app/account/page.tsx:1`. It has no description or canonical, and I left that alone for that reason.
- I read all 5 pages, the layout and navigation, `public/robots.txt`, `public/sitemap.xml`, `geo.config.json` and `package.json`. There are no JSON-LD sources, no middleware and no `next.config`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you want to apply the "Worth considering" ideas. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
